secretary.title: A word from the Secretary General
secretary.name: Rachid SOULAIMAN
secretary.role: Secretary General of Angham Al Andalous
paragraphs: Angham Al Andalous was born of a simple conviction: the Andalusian music of the Tlemcen school is not a memory to be kept under glass, but a living language passed on from voice to voice. In Sidi Bel Abbès, we want to give this heritage a place where it is played, heard and learned.

Our ambition is twofold: to keep the nouba and hawzi alive through musical evenings, meetings and exchanges with the Algiers and Constantine schools; and to document sources, works and their variants rigorously, so that future generations inherit reliable knowledge.
We walk in the footsteps of the masters. Whether you are a musician, a researcher, a music lover or the keeper of family archives, this house is yours too: I invite you to join us.

patrimoine.title: Musical heritage
patrimoine.intro: The history, forms and figures of Andalusian music from the Tlemcen school.
items: The Tlemcen school and its particularities
Transmission and preservation of the heritage
texts: From Ziryab in Córdoba to the Andalusian families welcomed in Tlemcen, the history of this music mixes established facts and handed-down stories. Our articles keep the two apart.
Tlemcen gave its name to one of Algeria’s three great schools, gharnati, with its own families of modes and its own repertoire.
The nouba, a great suite in five movements, and hawzi, poetry sung in dialectal Arabic, are the two pillars of the Tlemcen repertoire.
Rebab, kouitra, kamandja, tar and derbouka: a chamber ensemble in which every instrument ornaments the same melody.
From Cheikh Larbi Bensari to Abdelkrim Dali and Cheikha Tetma, the masters of the twentieth century carried this art far beyond Tlemcen.
Long handed down from master to pupil, this music reached radio, records and associations, from Tlemcen to Sidi Bel Abbès and beyond.

recherche.title: Research
recherche.intro: The association’s scientific approach and the results of its work.
items: Comparative studies and variants of works
texts: Our approach combines musical practice with the study of sources: every piece of information we publish is tied to its references, and debated points are presented as such.
Three lines guide our work: documenting musical sources, transcribing the works and comparing their versions.
We catalogue books, articles, manuscripts and recordings, and make them available in the site’s library, together with their terms of use.
In time we hope to offer musical transcriptions of the works, published only once checked and validated.
The same piece travels between Tlemcen, Algiers and Constantine in different forms: comparing these variants, titles and poems included, sheds light on their history.
Each work will have a record bringing together title variants, bibliographic sources, documented performances and authorised recordings, through a process of contribution and scientific validation.
The results of our work are published in Publications & news, starting with our in-depth articles on the Tlemcen school.

association.title: The association
association.intro: Who we are, what drives us and how we work.
texts: Angham Al Andalous is a cultural and scientific association from Sidi Bel Abbès, faithful to the Tlemcen school. Its motto, “In the footsteps of the masters”, expresses its commitment to transmission.
Our mission: to promote, preserve and pass on the Andalusian musical heritage of the Tlemcen school. Our vision: to become a reference platform, cultural and scientific, for this heritage.
To enliven cultural life with musical evenings, lectures and exchanges with the Algiers and Constantine schools; to document sources and support research.
